items.toString:
* Keep the partner-standard policy (600 req/min, burst 300) and give Globex Retail a second API key for the catalog export.
* Count bulk endpoints as one request per call (shop-api #412).
* Return cursor pagination hints in the 429 body of /search.
* Document the limits and headers in the partner API guide.
No impact on shop-api behaviour for other partners. Configuration and documentation only, tested on staging.

*Status codes*

* AC1: Traffic under the limit (UC-01) always gets 200.
* AC2: A burst of up to 300 requests (UC-02) gets 200; requests above the burst wait instead of failing.
* AC3: Sustained traffic over the limit (UC-03) gets 429 with {{Retry-After}} under 60 seconds.
* AC4: Two keys of the same partner (UC-04) are limited separately.
* AC5: A bulk call (UC-05) counts as one request.
* AC6: Webhook retries (UC-06) are never limited.
* AC7: Deep pagination (UC-07) is limited from page 151, and the error body suggests cursor pagination.
* AC8: An unknown key (UC-08) gets 401 and is not counted.

*Decision logic*

* AC9: The limit is read only from {{ratelimit.bucket}} of the API key. Neither the client IP nor {{X-Forwarded-For}} is used to decide.
* AC10: No configuration change raises the limit of every partner; the partner-standard policy stays as it is.

*Error handling*

* AC11: A 429 always has a JSON body with {{code: RATE_LIMITED}} and the reset time. It is never a 503 or an empty body.
* AC12: When Redis, which holds the buckets, is unavailable, requests are let through and an alert fires. The expected behaviour for bulk calls in that case still needs to be confirmed with Morgan Diaz.

*Evidence*

* AC13: All 11 cases have been run, and the result (status, error, rate-limit headers) is recorded in the results table of the ticket.

items.fromString:
h3. Test use cases — Globex Retail catalog sync on the public API

Common precondition: the partner uses its production API key against {{api.staging.acme-shop.example}}, with the *partner-standard* rate-limit policy. Each case is run with the load script attached to the ticket.

||ID||Scenario||Traffic||Expected status||Error shown||Additional check||
|UC-01|Single client under the limit|50 req/min to /search for 10 min|200|—|X-RateLimit-Remaining never reaches 0|
|UC-02|Burst at the start of a sync|400 requests in the first 5 s|200|—|The burst bucket (300) absorbs it; the rest wait under 1 s|
|UC-03|Sustained over the limit|900 req/min for 5 min|429|Rate limit exceeded|Retry-After is set and is under 60 s|
|UC-04|Two API keys of the same partner|2 × 400 req/min|200|—|The limit is per key, not per partner (see R2)|
|UC-05|Bulk price update|1 × POST /prices/bulk with 5 000 items|202|—|Counted as one request, not 5 000|
|UC-06|Webhook replay|200 webhook retries in 1 min|200|—|Webhook endpoints are not rate limited|
|UC-07|Search with deep pagination|page=1..200 in 30 s|429 from page 151|Rate limit exceeded|Cursor pagination is suggested in the error body|
|UC-08|Unknown API key|10 requests|401|Invalid API key|Not counted against any bucket|
|UC-09|Catalog export|GET /products?limit=500, 60 pages|200|—|Finishes in under 2 minutes|
|UC-10|Inventory poll|GET /inventory every 2 s|200|—|No 429 over 1 hour|
|UC-11|Mixed traffic at peak|Recorded Black Friday traffic, 3× speed|200 / 429|Rate limit exceeded|Fewer than 0.5% of requests get a 429|

h3. Rules that apply to every case

* R1: The limit is decided by the token bucket of the API key ({{ratelimit.bucket}}), never by the client IP; partners call from shared egress IPs.
* R2: Two keys of the same partner have separate buckets. A partner that needs more throughput asks for a second key, not a higher shared limit.
* R3: A 429 always carries {{Retry-After}} and {{X-RateLimit-Reset}}. An empty body or a 503 instead of a 429 is a failure.
* R4: Bulk endpoints count as one request per call. This is worth adding as UC-12: a bulk call with 50 000 items → expected status to be confirmed with the API owner.
* R5: Webhook and health endpoints are never rate limited.

fields.summary: Find the rate-limit configuration that gives the partner the behaviour they expect.

content.text: The partner just replied with the details below, and I attached the load script they shared:
They will run their catalog sync against staging with the attached script, covering every pattern they expect us to support.
They need an answer by Monday morning on whether a configuration exists that gives them the behaviour below.
Their go-live is next week, so they
wait for a code change on our side.
The traffic patterns and what they expect are in their guide:
: 60 req/min, each call counts as one

policies:
  partner-standard:
    rate: 600/min
    burst: 300
    key: api_key
  partner-bulk:
    rate: 60/min
    burst: 10
    key: api_key
I ran all 11 cases on staging:
UC-01 to UC-06, UC-08 to UC-10
: 429 from page 151 as expected, but the body has no pagination hint yet.
: 0.3% of requests got a 429, under the 0.5% target.
I will share this with the partner today.
The partner confirmed the results. Two follow-ups from them:
Can the second API key be issued
Can the 429 body name the bucket that ran out?
The second key is issued and shared through the partner portal.
The 429 body now names the bucket (shop-api #415, on staging).
